YOUR SONG. YOUR STAGE.

Choose a background

Use your own Guitar Hero Metallica gameplay footage, music video or concert clip. H.264 MP4 / WebM is recommended. Videos up to 500 MB can save on this device; larger videos play for this session. The video stays local and muted; your song supplies the audio.

Use a YouTube link (youtu.be, watch, Shorts or embed) or a direct HTTPS MP4/WebM video link. Vimeo and other video-page links are not supported. Linked videos stay muted and follow the same chart timing. They need internet access; saving keeps the link, not the video file.

No video selected for this song.

YouTube selected. Use Preview timing with chart to check it. Its thumbnail stays still until the first note; buffering can delay playback. YouTube must allow embedded playback and may show ads. Its available practice speeds vary by video. Upload a video file for the most precise timing and offline playback.

File and direct-link videos preview here. For YouTube, use Preview timing with chart to see it behind the notes. The starting position follows the timing below.

The video stays paused until the first note reaches the colored hit line, in Preview chart and Play track. Enter 0 to start at the beginning of your video, or 10 to skip its first 10 seconds. A negative number delays video playback further. Pause, restart and practice follow the chart.

Video starts at 0:00 when the first note reaches the hit line.

Replays the lead-in to the first note with your selected instrument, difficulty and video timing. No score is saved. Open Backgrounds / video again to adjust and retry.

Keep this video and its timing with the song in your setlist on this device. It loads again when you reopen the song. Uploaded files can play offline; linked videos require internet access. Videos up to 2 GB can be saved if there is enough free browser storage.

Save the selected video, timing, song audio and all charts together in one .riffpack file. Import it through Manage songs to restore them. Video limit: 2 GB. For linked videos, the backup includes the URL and timing instead of video bytes and needs internet access. Regular Export current song keeps the smaller chart-and-audio backup.

Videos up to 500 MB also save automatically. For larger videos, choose Save video to setlist after selecting or importing them. Keep a combined backup too; clearing this game’s browser data removes saved songs and videos.
GROW YOUR SETLIST

Add a song

Enter a song title and artist to find its chart and bundled audio when available. No audio upload is needed. You can also upload audio to chart your own recording.

No file needed: enter song title and artist below to find its chart and audio.

Matching Guitar Hero conversions are preferred. GH1–3 supply Guitar only; Drums require an actual drum chart from a later game or the community. Uploads must match source audio. Clone Hero Drum charts can also be verified with full-song-only packages. Verified saved charts are reused for the same audio. Missing Drum charts can use verified isolated Drum audio for an estimate; other missing parts use the song audio. If your selected instrument has no matching chart, the lookup shows which other parts are available.

Searches downloadable MusicXML scores on Internet Archive after game charts, separately for Guitar, Drums, Bass and Vocals. Converts the parts actually written in the score into colored lanes and four difficulties. Availability varies; missing parts can still use audio estimates.

Use an uncompressed MusicXML export up to 4 MB, with a starting tempo and repeats written out. PDFs, photos and compressed MXL need a MusicXML export first. Score notes need timing review against your recording. Without audio, available score parts can be saved and previewed as a chart only.

Every upload searches matching community charts first when this option is on. Imported backups also check their estimated parts using the backup’s saved song title and artist. Use an Artist - Title filename or fill in both fields for new audio. Audio stays on your device.

Missing Guitar, Bass, Drums and Vocals parts are searched independently. Working authored charts saved with this recording keep their notes, difficulties and timing. Riffbound checks song length and tries other matching charts for missing parts. Parts without a usable chart use audio estimates.

With title and artist only, we’ll search Guitar Hero / Clone Hero charts and retrieve the matching song audio when available. If your chosen instrument has no supported chart, we’ll make an estimate from that song audio. Each part stays separate. If audio is unavailable, supported charts can still be saved and you can attach matching audio later.

MP3, WAV, M4A, OGG, FLAC and other audio your browser can open. 5 seconds–15 minutes, up to 80 MB per song. Saved on this device; no song links needed.

Automatic charts are estimates. Preview the notes before playing; isolated instruments give clearer results.

YOUR NOTES. YOUR ARRANGEMENT.

Chart files

Import a .chart or notes.mid file with its matching audio. Authored Guitar, Bass, Drums and pitched MIDI Vocals are supported. Supplied difficulty levels are kept.

Use song.ini from the same Clone Hero chart folder to include its chart delay, drum layout and MIDI hold settings.

Positive values move notes later in the audio. Tempo changes, the chart’s own offset and song.ini delay are included. Use the exact recording from that chart for the closest match.

Choose a chart to see its instruments, difficulties and note counts.

Supplied non-empty difficulties replace those levels for the matching audio. Other saved levels and instruments stay as they are. For a new part, missing levels are derived from the closest supplied arrangement and labeled generated.

Fretted notes, chords, holds and individual drum hits are supported. Open frets, sustained drum rolls, unpitched vocals and six-fret charts are not imported. MIDI Vocals use pitch pads, without microphone scoring. HOPO/tap, accent and phrase markings use Riffbound’s normal gameplay.

Export the open song

Export notes for editing. Keep the matching audio beside the chart; use Manage songs for a complete .riffpack backup.

REPEAT. IMPROVE.

Practice a section

Play a fill or solo and see your section result. Section bests stay separate from full-song scores. Use Retry or press R to restart the same section with a fresh count-in.

Named ranges save with this song in your setlist and .riffpack backups.

By default, the section ends with your percentage and score. Practice again repeats the same section and speed. Slower playback also lowers the audio pitch. Highway speed changes note spacing without changing the song.
MATCH YOUR DEVICE

Timing calibration

Use the speakers or headphones you play with. Listen to the clicks, then tap in time with them. Keep tapping for the whole test.

Twelve beats. The first two help you settle into the rhythm.

Positive values give your taps more time; negative values move the hit window earlier. This adjusts playback timing, not which drum a color represents.

Feedback shows successful hits relative to the chart after calibration. It does not change scoring or adjust timing automatically.
TAKE THE STAGE WITH YOU

Install & play offline

Game updates download automatically while online and apply when you are between songs with your work saved. Open a saved In Bloom or matching Roam drum track to receive its latest chart corrections. Songs stay on this device and can be opened offline.

On iPhone, open this link in Safari, then Share → Add to Home Screen. On Android, use your browser’s Install or Add to Home Screen option.

Keep a .riffpack backup of songs you want to keep. Clearing browser data removes local songs and the offline copy.
SOUNDCHECK

Find your rhythm.

Colored notes travel down the highway. Play them when they reach the glowing fret line near the bottom.

Choose Guitar, Drums, Bass or Vocals beside the chart. Switching parts during play restarts the track with a fresh score. While paused, choose a part and press Play. Preview switches keep your position.

For a drum kit, guitar controller, gamepad or MIDI device, open Controllers / drums at Soundcheck. Assign each pad and pedal, test the inputs, then return to play. Four- and five-lane drum mappings save separately.

  1. Auto-chart your songChoose Guitar, Drums, Bass or Vocals above the upload button, then upload a full song or isolated track. Whole song builds all four charts; Separate parts builds the parts you check. Each part has its own preview and highway; the original song plays in every mode. Changing instruments rebuilds the song separately. Pick Easy, Medium, Hard or Expert, then choose Preview chart to watch the notes play automatically. Move Preview from to hear another part. Choose Play track or Play yourself when you are ready.
  2. Tap fretsPress D F J K L for green, red, yellow, blue, and orange. On a phone, tap the colored fret buttons.
  3. Hold + strumHold the matching fret keys, then press Enter at the right moment. Hold all the matching frets for chords.
  4. Play a vocal melodyVocal pitch runs from low to high across the five colors. Tap D F J K L or the matching pads and hold long notes. This mode charts the melody for pad play; it does not use your microphone or recognize lyrics. Other pitched instruments in a full recording can affect the estimate.
  5. Keep it ringingHold a fret through a long note's tail for extra points. Build a streak to reach a 4× multiplier.
  6. Play the drumsClone Hero community charts use four lanes: D red, F yellow, J blue, K green, with no orange pad. Guitar Hero drum charts keep five lanes. Their lanes run left to right: D — red snare, F — yellow closed/open hi-hat, J — blue tom, K — orange cymbal, and L — green floor tom. The green pad / L also hits orange cymbal notes; one green hit covers orange and green notes arriving together. Press Space or Enter for wide purple kick bars. Alternate both keys for fast kicks, or use the wide touch pedal. Play other simultaneous notes together. On a phone, tap the matching ring or the kick pedal.
  7. Unleash OverdriveAt 50% charge, press Shift on drums, Space on Guitar, Bass or Vocals, or the Overdrive button to double your multiplier. Escape or Pause opens Resume, Practice, Restart, Change difficulty and Quit. Changing difficulty restarts the song or practice section with a fresh score.

Easy uses fewer notes and simpler rhythms; Medium adds more notes; Hard adds denser fills and chords; Expert keeps every distinct detected note from the audio; Hard, Medium and Easy are reduced from that full chart. Rebuild an existing song’s instrument chart to apply updated audio charting. Guitar and Bass use three frets on Easy, four on Medium, and five on Hard/Expert. Drum lane colors follow the source layout: four pads for Clone Hero community charts, five for Guitar Hero drum charts. Vocal melody keeps its five pitch colors. Space or Enter plays the drum kick; Shift activates drum Overdrive. This is free play: missed notes lower crowd energy, but the song keeps going. Practice can select the last missed section and play it at 25–100% speed in 5% steps. Retry or R restarts the current song or practice section. Early/late feedback shows successful hit timing; turn it off in Timing if you prefer. The built-in track uses original synthesized music. Uploaded charts estimate instrument parts from the mixed audio; they are not exact transcriptions.

Connect. Assign. Play.

Connect your drum kit, guitar or gamepad to Windows, then press a button. Use your device’s USB cable, compatible wireless receiver, or USB-MIDI interface. Riffbound can read devices your browser detects; it cannot replace a missing hardware adapter.

Built-in setups load when a supported device connects.

Standard gamepads have controls ready for Guitar, Bass, vocal pitch pads and both drum layouts. Recognized standard-mapped Guitar Hero drum kits and guitars load their instrument setup automatically. If Windows gives your Xbox kit a generic controller name, select Guitar Hero Xbox 360 drums once above. MIDI drums load their General MIDI assignments after you enable access. The song selects its four- or five-lane layout automatically.

LIVE INPUT TEST

Waiting for a hit…

Assigned rows flash when you hit them. Testing here does not score or play the song.

World Tour Xbox 360 preset: choose a controller that Windows exposes with standard button mapping and the five-lane drum layout. Orange cymbal and kick use separate inputs. Xbox 360 wireless drums require their PC receiver for this route, as in Guitar Hero World Tour on PC. For other mappings or MIDI, assign the controls individually.

Custom mapping is optional for supported setups. To customize, choose Add input, strike one pad, cymbal or pedal and release it. Some kits send a button combination for one pad. You can add alternate inputs to the same action. MIDI pitch pads use C4, D4, E4, F4, G4; C5 strums, D5 activates Overdrive, E5 pauses. Vocal mode plays pitch pads and does not score microphone singing. MIDI requires browser permission; desktop Chrome or Edge is recommended. Unknown device layouts need custom mapping. Stage Tour hardware compatibility still needs testing with a physical kit.
